title: SOP-CONV-05: Main Assembly Line Conveyor Belt Misalignment Troubleshooting
section: 1. System Overview and Pinch Point Hazard Warning
content:
1. System Overview and Pinch Point Hazard Warning
This procedure specifies corrective measures for tracking deviation, lateral drift, and edge rub on heavy-duty motorized modular conveyor system **CV-02** (Packaging Line 1).
**WARNING: MOVING EQUIPMENT HAZARD.** Never place hands, fingers, or loose clothing within 500 mm of the head or tail pulley pinch zones while the conveyor is in motion. Maintenance guards **MG-01** and **MG-02** may only be removed during static alignment or when utilizing extended adjustment handles.

title: SOP-CONV-05: Main Assembly Line Conveyor Belt Misalignment Troubleshooting
section: 2. Fault Indication and Tracking Sensor Diagnostic
content:
2. Fault Indication and Tracking Sensor Diagnostic
1. An off-center belt tracking condition is automatically flagged when the belt edge triggers inductive proximity sensor **PRX-TRK-L** (left limit) or **PRX-TRK-R** (right limit), producing alarm **E-315: Conveyor CV-02 Lateral Belt Tracking Deviation Exceeded (+/- 25 mm)**.
2. If drift exceeds 35 mm, the fail-safe conveyor tracking safety switch **SS-TRK-01** trips, causing an immediate automated line interlock stop.
3. Inspect the fault beacon at Station 4: a pulsing red beacon confirms conveyor trip due to E-315.
4. Record the belt travel direction and drift orientation (drive side or idle side) in the maintenance terminal.

title: SOP-CONV-05: Main Assembly Line Conveyor Belt Misalignment Troubleshooting
section: 3. Initial Static Inspection and Debris Check
content:
3. Initial Static Inspection and Debris Check
Before adjusting mechanical tracking tensioners:
1. De-energize conveyor CV-02 following standard LOTO per SOP-SAF-02. Lock main conveyor disconnect switch **DS-CV02**.
2. Inspect the underside return idler rollers (**IDL-01** through **IDL-12**) for packaging tape, strap fragments, or cardboard build-up. Accumulation as thin as 2 mm on an idler drum creates conical diameter variance that drives the belt sideways.
3. Clean all idlers and snub rollers with brass scraper **SC-BR02** and lint-free solvent cloths.
4. Inspect the belt surface for cupping, torn edge lace fasteners (Clipper wire hooks or Alligator staple fasteners), or longitudinal gouges.

title: SOP-CONV-05: Main Assembly Line Conveyor Belt Misalignment Troubleshooting
content:
4. Mechanical Tracking Adjustment Procedure
Conveyor belt tracking must be corrected by adjusting the take-up bearing position on the tail pulley assembly:
1. Loosen the four jam nuts on take-up bearing blocks **BB-TAIL-L** and **BB-TAIL-R** using a 24 mm open-end box wrench **WR-24**.
2. Identify rule of tracking: *The belt moves toward the side of the idler or pulley that it contacts first.*
3. If the belt drifts to the **Left (Operator Side)**:
   - Turn the left tensioning threaded screw **TS-01L** clockwise by exactly 1/2 turn (180 degrees) to increase tension on the left side, pushing the belt back toward center.
   - Alternatively, turn the right tensioning screw **TS-01R** counter-clockwise by 1/2 turn.
4. If the belt drifts to the **Right (Drive Side)**:
   - Turn the right tensioning threaded screw **TS-01R** clockwise by 1/2 turn.
5. Use laser alignment collimator **LAT-01** magnetically attached to the tail pulley shaft to verify pulley squareness is within 0.05 degrees (1 mm per meter of pulley width).

title: SOP-CONV-05: Main Assembly Line Conveyor Belt Misalignment Troubleshooting
section: 5. Dynamic Run Test and Final Verification
content:
5. Dynamic Run Test and Final Verification
1. Clear all tools, remove LOTO padlocks, and restore power.
2. Station an observer at Emergency Stop station PB-04 with finger poised on the E-Stop button.
3. Start conveyor CV-02 in low-speed jog mode (25% nominal velocity, 0.25 m/s) and allow the belt to complete 3 full revolutions (approx. 90 seconds).
4. Observe the belt edge position relative to the reference center scribe lines on guide plate **GP-01**.
5. Once belt tracks true within +/- 3 mm of center at full operating speed (1.0 m/s) for 10 minutes continuously, tighten all four 24 mm jam nuts on the bearing blocks to 85 Nm torque using torque wrench **TW-100**.
6. Reset alarm E-315 on the main packaging cell HMI.

title: SOP-ENV-04: Industrial Coolant Leak Containment and Emergency Response
content:
1. Initial Assessment and Hazard Identification
This standard operating procedure defines the immediate containment, cleanup, and reporting protocols for water-soluble and synthetic cutting coolant leaks from machining centers CNC-01 through CNC-08.
**ENVIRONMENTAL & SLIP HAZARD:** Coolant mixtures (specifically Cimcool Cimtech 410) pose high slip-and-fall hazards and potential skin sensitization. Prevent any coolant runoff from entering floor drains or stormwater outlets. Wear chemical splash goggles, neoprene gloves (EN 374), and slip-resistant rubber safety overboots.

title: SOP-ENV-04: Industrial Coolant Leak Containment and Emergency Response
section: 2. Emergency Isolation and Leak Source Stoppage
content:
2. Emergency Isolation and Leak Source Stoppage
When a coolant leak is observed or annunciated by fault code **E-412: Coolant Delivery System Pressure Loss (< 1.5 bar)**:
1. Immediately press the **Feed Hold** button and turn off high-pressure coolant pump selector **SW-PMP-01** at the operator pendant.
2. If the leak originates from a ruptured high-pressure flex hose, press Emergency Stop **PB-01** to de-energize the entire fluid circuit.
3. Close the manual quarter-turn quarter-inch stainless ball valve **V-CLT-SUPPLY** on the main reservoir feeder to isolate fluid delivery.
4. Notify the environmental compliance officer and maintenance lead via plant radio channel 3.

title: SOP-ENV-04: Industrial Coolant Leak Containment and Emergency Response
content:
3. Spill Containment and Barrier Deployment
1. Retrieve Mobile Spill Response Kit **SK-01** stationed at Bay C column 14.
2. Deploy yellow polypropylene absorbent socks (**SK-SOCK-03**) completely encircling the fluid perimeter to prevent spread toward floor drain **DR-04**.
3. Place absorbent drain seal mat (**MAT-DR-01**) directly over floor drain DR-04 and stomp firmly to create a watertight vacuum seal against the concrete substrate.
4. Surround the leaking machine enclosure with universal absorbent pads (**PAD-UNV-50**), overlapping pad edges by at least 50 mm.
5. If fluid accumulation exceeds 20 liters, deploy the air-operated diaphragm portable transfer pump (**PMP-TRANS-AODD**) and direct the discharge wand into marked polyethylene salvage drum **DRUM-CLT-WASTE**.

title: SOP-ENV-04: Industrial Coolant Leak Containment and Emergency Response
section: 4. Hose and Fitting Inspection and Repair Verification
content:
4. Hose and Fitting Inspection and Repair Verification
1. Inspect high-pressure braided coolant lines (**CH-01** through **CH-04**) for puncture, crimp fitting slippage, or abrasive wear against the machine chassis.
2. Check Quick-Disconnect couplers (**QD-CLT-8**) for degraded Buna-N O-rings. If worn, replace O-ring with part number **OR-BN70-112**.
3. Check filter canister **FLT-CLT-20** for clogged 20-micron filter element. A differential pressure indicator reading in the red zone (> 2.2 bar) indicates filter rupture risks. Replace element with **EL-20M-SYN**.
4. Tighten all flare fittings to 28 Nm using calibrated torque wrench **TW-50**.

title: SOP-ENV-04: Industrial Coolant Leak Containment and Emergency Response
content:
5. Decontamination, Disposal, and Coolant Recharge
1. Collect all saturated absorbent pads and containment socks using spark-proof brass shovel **SH-BR01**. Place spent absorbents into heavy-duty 6-mil hazardous waste bags **BAG-HAZ-YW**.
2. Label waste bags with "SPENT SYNTHETIC COOLANT - CIMTECH 410" and deposit in designated Hazardous Waste Collection Area H-2.
3. Clean the floor with biodegradable floor degreaser **DEG-BIO-10** and industrial wet-vacuum **VAC-WET-02**. Ensure the surface passes the dry-friction slip test before removing warning cones.
4. Refill coolant reservoir with 8% pre-mixed refractometer-verified coolant (Brix index 8.2 on optical refractometer **RF-OPT-01**).
5. Clear alarm code E-412 on HMI and run coolant pump dry-cycle test for 3 minutes to verify zero line leakage at 25 bar operating pressure.

title: SOP-OPS-03: Daily Pre-Shift Equipment Inspection and Operational Checklist
content:
1. Objective and Pre-Operational Safety
This standard operating procedure outlines the mandatory 20-minute daily pre-shift inspection required on all automated production lines prior to starting shift operations.
**SAFETY DIRECTIVE:** Wear mandatory personal protective equipment (PPE): ANSI Z87.1 approved impact safety glasses, steel-toe boots (ASTM F2413), and cut-resistant nitrile-dipped gloves (ANSI Cut Level A3). Never bypass safety interlock switches during pre-shift visual inspections.

title: SOP-OPS-03: Daily Pre-Shift Equipment Inspection and Operational Checklist
content:
2. Emergency Stop and Interlock Verification
Before power is applied to main motor drives:
1. Walk the perimeter of the production line and physically inspect all 6 Emergency Stop mushroom buttons (**E-Stop PB-01** through **PB-06**).
2. Confirm each E-Stop button is free of physical damage, cracks, or mechanical sticking.
3. Test the emergency trip wire on the primary discharge conveyor by pulling firmly with a force of 40-50 N. Verify that safety relay module **SR-101** trips and illuminates the amber fault LED.
4. Verify all interlocked polycarbonate safety doors (**G-1** through **G-6**): open each door individually and verify that safety circuit breaker **CB-SAFE** immediately opens, showing status "INTERLOCK OPEN" on the central annunciator.
5. Inspect optical safety light curtains (**LC-OPT-A** and **LC-OPT-B**) at the palletizing infeed. Pass a 30 mm test rod through the beam array and verify drive motor contactors instantaneously drop out.

title: SOP-OPS-03: Daily Pre-Shift Equipment Inspection and Operational Checklist
content:
3. Fluid Levels, Pressures, and Lubrication
1. **Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU-1):** Check the sight glass on reservoir **TK-HYD-01**. Fluid level must sit between the 65% and 80% marks. Fluid must appear clear amber; if milky (water contamination) or dark brown (oxidation), log maintenance alert **AL-OIL-02**. Check reservoir temperature gauge **TI-201**; normal operating range is 38°C to 52°C.
2. **Pneumatic Main Pressure:** Inspect primary regulator gauge **REG-PN-01**. Operating line pressure must read between 6.0 and 6.5 bar (87-94 psi). Drain automatic moisture trap filter **FLT-H2O-01** by pressing the bottom purge valve until clear air expels.
3. **Automatic Central Lubricator:** Verify grease canister **LUB-AUTO-01** contains approved synthetic lithium complex grease (Mobilux EP 2). Level must exceed minimum fill line (minimum 250 mL). Verify lubricant delivery pressure gauge reads 15-20 bar during cyclic pulse.

title: SOP-OPS-03: Daily Pre-Shift Equipment Inspection and Operational Checklist
section: 4. Mechanical Drive, Belts, and Fastener Inspection
content:
4. Mechanical Drive, Belts, and Fastener Inspection
1. Inspect main drive transmission belts for tension using sonic tension tester **STT-01** or finger deflection method (maximum permissible deflection is 8 mm under 20 N applied load). Check for fraying, edge cracking, or rubber shavings.
2. Inspect primary drive chains for slack and ensure automatic oil drip applicator **DRP-02** is delivering 2 drops per minute.
3. Check motor mounting bolts and pillow-block bearings (**PB-B101** through **PB-B108**) with handheld infrared thermometer **Fluke-62MAX**. Bearing surface temperatures must not exceed 65°C during idling.

title: SOP-OPS-03: Daily Pre-Shift Equipment Inspection and Operational Checklist
section: 5. Shift Sign-Off and HMI Readiness Log
content:
5. Shift Sign-Off and HMI Readiness Log
1. Navigate to the HMI **Main Menu > Shift Handover > Pre-Shift Inspection Checklist**.
2. Input operator badge number, shift number (Shift 1, 2, or 3), and confirm all check items.
3. If any critical safety anomaly is detected (e.g. defective E-Stop, low hydraulic oil below 50%, or light curtain failure), DO NOT START LINE. Immediately place out-of-service tag on panel and summon the maintenance team.
4. If all items pass, click **Authorize Shift Start** to enable machine cycle controls.

title: SOP-SAF-02: Hazardous Energy Control - Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
content:
1. Scope and Life-Safety Warning
This procedure mandates the strict isolation of all electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and stored mechanical energy sources prior to any maintenance, cleaning, servicing, or unjamming activities on plant machinery.
**DANGER: ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY.** Servicing energized machinery without completing formal Lockout/Tagout constitutes an immediate OSHA violation and poses lethal arc-flash, electrocution, or amputation risks. Every authorized technician must apply their personal red padlock and danger tag. Master or gang keys are strictly forbidden.

title: SOP-SAF-02: Hazardous Energy Control - Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
content:
2. Equipment Preparation and Notification
Before initiating mechanical isolation:
1. Identify all primary and secondary energy sources feeding the target machine:
   - Primary 480V AC 3-phase high voltage electrical feed.
   - Auxiliary 24V DC control power transformer bus.
   - Plant pneumatic compressed air supply line (8.0 bar / 116 psi).
   - High-pressure hydraulic accumulator circuit (160 bar).
2. Verbally notify the shift production supervisor, line operators, and adjacent cell workers that the equipment is being removed from service.
3. Execute standard operational shutdown via the primary control panel by pressing the **Stop** button and allowing internal drives to brake to zero RPM.

title: SOP-SAF-02: Hazardous Energy Control - Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
content:
3. Sequential Isolation and Energy Dissipation
Execute isolation strictly in the following order:
1. **Electrical Disconnect:** Open the primary rotary electrical isolator switch located on Main Power Distribution Cabinet **MDB-01**. Throw switch handle from the vertical ON position to horizontal OFF.
2. **Pneumatic Lockout:** Locate main air shutoff ball valve **V-AIR-01**. Turn handle 90 degrees perpendicular to the supply pipe. Slide the exhaust slide sleeve forward to vent all downstream air with an audible discharge hiss.
3. **Hydraulic De-energization:** Close high-pressure isolation valve **HYD-ISO-04**. Depress manual bleed valve **PB-BLEED-HYD** until pressure gauge **PG-H02** reads exactly 0.0 bar.
4. **Gravitational Restraint:** Lower all mechanical counterweights, ram presses, or pneumatic lift cylinders to the physical bottom stop, or insert steel safety drop-pins **PIN-STL-50**.

title: SOP-SAF-02: Hazardous Energy Control - Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
section: 4. Padlock, Hasps, and Danger Tag Application
content:
4. Padlock, Hasps, and Danger Tag Application
1. Place a heavy-duty nylon safety hasp **HSP-06** through the padlock hole of rotary switch MDB-01.
2. Affix your assigned OSHA-compliant red personal safety padlock **PL-RED-01** through the hasp hole. Retain the single unique key in your personal possession.
3. Affix Lockout Tag **TAG-DNG-01** filled out completely with: Authorized Operator Name, Employee ID, Cell / Line Name, Date, Contact Phone Extension, and Reason for Lockout.
4. Affix secondary lockout clamshell bracket **LC-PN-02** around pneumatic ball valve V-AIR-01 and lock with a second red padlock.

title: SOP-SAF-02: Hazardous Energy Control - Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
content:
5. Zero-Energy Verification ("Try-Step")
Never assume isolation is effective without performing mandatory physical verification:
1. Using calibrated digital multimeter **Fluke-87V** (verified on a known live voltage source immediately prior), test line-to-line (L1-L2, L2-L3, L1-L3) and line-to-ground for zero volts AC (<3.0V AC residual).
2. Verify visual pressure gauges **PG-A01** (pneumatics) and **PG-H02** (hydraulics) read absolute zero.
3. Press the machine **Start** pushbutton on the local operator console for 5 seconds. Verify that no contactor clicks, motor hums, or motion occurs.
4. Return the control switch to the **Off** position. The machine is now verified safe for servicing.

title: SOP-M03-01: Machine 3 - Clearing Feed-Roller Jam and Restart Procedure
content:
1. Scope and Safety Warnings
This standard operating procedure applies exclusively to automated thermoforming Machine 3 (Line B) when material feeding stalls or optical feed sensors detect roller slippage. When an obstruction halts feed-roller rotation, the human-machine interface (HMI) trips into critical shutdown mode.
**WARNING: HAZARDOUS MECHANICAL PINCH POINT.** Never reach into the roller housing while drive servos are energized. Always engage the emergency stop button (E-Stop PB-03) or perform standard lockout/tagout (LOTO) per SOP-SAF-02 before opening enclosure guard G-3. Failure to de-energize mechanical rollers can result in severe crushing injuries.

title: SOP-M03-01: Machine 3 - Clearing Feed-Roller Jam and Restart Procedure
section: 2. Initial Shutdown and E-204 Error Code Verification
content:
2. Initial Shutdown and E-204 Error Code Verification
When a feed jam occurs, Machine 3 emits an intermittent 90 dB acoustic beacon and illuminates the amber warning tower.
1. Check the primary operator control console for active fault diagnostic code **E-204: Feed Roller Tachometer Desynchronization / Stall Detection**.
2. Press the red mushroom-head Emergency Stop switch **PB-03** on the infeed operator panel.
3. Verify on the HMI screen that servo bus DC voltage discharges to below 50V DC before approaching the safety interlocking doors.
4. Record the timestamp, roll lot number, and fault status code E-204 in the shift operating logbook.

title: SOP-M03-01: Machine 3 - Clearing Feed-Roller Jam and Restart Procedure
content:
3. Feed-Roller Jam Clearance Procedure
Follow these sequential manual clearance instructions:
1. Open interlocked guard door **G-3** using universal key wrench T-12.
2. Locate the pneumatic tension release lever (labeled **VALVE-PR-3**) mounted directly beneath the upper drive arbor.
3. Rotate VALVE-PR-3 counter-clockwise 90 degrees to vent residual pneumatic pressure (regulated at 6.2 bar) and separate the upper nip-roller from the driven hardened steel feed-roller.
4. Utilizing non-marring brass pry wedge **TL-BR08** and high-tensile safety shears **SH-04**, slice the bunched raw polymer sheet along the transverse groove guide.
5. Manually pull the jammed material rearward away from the drive teeth. Do not strike the ceramic-coated rollers with hardened steel tools or screwdrivers.

title: SOP-M03-01: Machine 3 - Clearing Feed-Roller Jam and Restart Procedure
content:
4. Roller Inspection and Debris Removal
1. Inspect the upper and lower roller surfaces using inspection lamp **FL-02**. Ensure no melted plastic, stray tape, or carbonized residue adheres to the knurled roller surface.
2. If roller contamination exists, apply approved industrial solvent **Solv-80** onto lint-free microfiber cloth **CL-14** and wipe roller cylinders until clean. Allow 2 minutes for solvent evaporation.
3. Check the feed roller gap gauge: using metric feeler gauge **FG-05**, verify clearance is calibrated to exactly 2.4 mm (+/- 0.1 mm) across both drive ends.

title: SOP-M03-01: Machine 3 - Clearing Feed-Roller Jam and Restart Procedure
section: 5. Machine 3 Restart and HMI Fault Reset Protocol
content:
5. Machine 3 Restart and HMI Fault Reset Protocol
Once the feed path is free of obstruction:
1. Return pneumatic tension release lever VALVE-PR-3 clockwise 90 degrees until the pressure gauge reads 6.2 bar.
2. Close and latch interlocked safety door G-3. Verify the magnetic interlock switch indicator changes from flashing amber to solid green.
3. Pull to release Emergency Stop PB-03.
4. On the HMI touchscreen, navigate to **Diagnostics > Alarms**, select active alarm **E-204**, and tap **Acknowledge and Clear**.
5. Depress the blue **Master Control Relay (MCR) Reset** pushbutton for 3 continuous seconds.
6. Switch the operating selector switch to **Jog Feed Mode**, advance 0.5 meters of test material, and observe roller rotation.
7. If material advances smoothly without tracking skew, press the green **Cycle Start** pushbutton to resume automated production.

title: SOP-CAL-06: Robotic Spindle Rotary Torque Sensor Calibration Protocol
content:
1. Scope, Purpose, and Metrology Standards
This standard operating procedure prescribes the semi-annual static calibration and zero-drift verification for the high-precision rotary strain-gauge torque transducer (**Model Futek TRS-605 / Tag TQ-104**) installed on Automated Fastening Spindle **SP-02** (Cell 3).
**CRITICAL QUALITY NOTICE:** Accurate torque feedback is essential to prevent overtightening and stripped threads on automotive battery tray fasteners. Calibration must comply with ISO 6789-2:2017 standards. All calibration weights and digital indicators must hold current NIST-traceable accreditation certificates.

title: SOP-CAL-06: Robotic Spindle Rotary Torque Sensor Calibration Protocol
content:
2. Pre-Calibration Setup and Thermal Stabilization
1. Ensure Cell 3 environmental conditions are stable: ambient temperature must be 20°C +/- 2°C (68°F +/- 3.6°F) and relative humidity between 35% and 65%. Record environmental readings from thermo-hygrometer **TH-03**.
2. De-energize spindle drive motor per SOP-SAF-02. Lock out high-voltage servo amp breaker **CB-SP02**. Leave low-voltage 24V DC sensor instrumentation power active.
3. Power on digital torque signal conditioning amplifier **AMP-TQ-02** and allow a 30-minute warm-up stabilization period to prevent thermal zero drift.
4. If diagnostic fault **E-508: Torque Transducer Static Zero Offset Exceeded (> 1.2% Full Scale)** is active on the cell controller, note the raw bridge output voltage in mV/V.

title: SOP-CAL-06: Robotic Spindle Rotary Torque Sensor Calibration Protocol
section: 3. Shunt Calibration and Zero Balance Verification
content:
3. Shunt Calibration and Zero Balance Verification
1. Inspect the physical condition of torque transducer TQ-104: check the slip-ring housing, cable shielding **CBL-TQ-SH**, and M12 8-pin IP67 circular connector. Clean connector contacts with contact cleaner **CRC-2000** if oxidation is visible.
2. With zero mechanical load on spindle SP-02, navigate on amplifier AMP-TQ-02 to **Channel 1 > Calibration > Zero Tare**.
3. Measure the zero-load sensor voltage across pins 2 and 3 using calibrated 6.5-digit multimeter **Agilent-34401A**. Voltage must read 0.000 mV +/- 0.025 mV.
4. Activate the internal precision shunt resistor (350.0 kΩ, 0.01% tolerance) by pressing the **CAL SHUNT** button. The displayed reading must register 80.00% of nominal full-scale (equivalent to 40.00 Nm on a 50 Nm transducer) within +/- 0.10 Nm.

title: SOP-CAL-06: Robotic Spindle Rotary Torque Sensor Calibration Protocol
content:
4. Five-Point Deadweight Static Load Calibration
Execute a 5-point calibration test using certified NIST-traceable calibration arm **CAL-ARM-50** (exactly 0.5000 meters effective length) and class F deadweights:
1. Mount CAL-ARM-50 onto the square drive output shaft of spindle SP-02. Level the arm horizontally using precision digital spirit level **DL-01** (angular tilt < 0.05 degrees).
2. Apply the following clockwise test loads sequentially, pausing 30 seconds at each step:
   - **Point 1 (10 Nm):** Suspend certified weight hanger plus 2.039 kg mass (**WT-02**). Target reading: 10.00 Nm (Permissible range: 9.95 to 10.05 Nm).
   - **Point 2 (20 Nm):** Add 2.039 kg mass. Target reading: 20.00 Nm (Range: 19.90 to 20.10 Nm).
   - **Point 3 (30 Nm):** Add 2.039 kg mass. Target reading: 30.00 Nm (Range: 29.85 to 30.15 Nm).
   - **Point 4 (40 Nm):** Add 2.039 kg mass. Target reading: 40.00 Nm (Range: 39.80 to 40.20 Nm).
   - **Point 5 (50 Nm - Full Scale):** Add final mass. Target reading: 50.00 Nm (Range: 49.75 to 50.25 Nm).
3. Repeat the procedure in descending order to calculate hysteresis error. Maximum allowable hysteresis across all points is 0.25% FS (0.125 Nm).

title: SOP-CAL-06: Robotic Spindle Rotary Torque Sensor Calibration Protocol
section: 5. Calibration Sign-Off, Gain Adjustment, and Certification
content:
5. Calibration Sign-Off, Gain Adjustment, and Certification
1. If any point deviates beyond +/- 0.5% FS, adjust calibration gain potentiometer **POT-GAIN-01** or input digital slope coefficient in firmware menu **Setup > Scaling > Cal Factor**.
2. Save the calibration profile to internal EEPROM.
3. Affix tamper-evident calibration sticker **LBL-CAL-PASS** on transducer housing TQ-104 displaying: Date Calibrated, Calibration Due Date (6 months), Technician Initials, and Certificate Number **CAL-2026-TQ104**.
4. Clear fault code E-508 on the robotic controller, re-enable spindle servo drive, and perform 3 test fastening cycles on torque verification test block **TB-FAST-01**.
